label: At D1 late in episodes, fires after a common a1->S1 trial, more when unrewarded.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action + prev_state == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial/12) ;; (phase == D1) * np.exp(ep_trial/12) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial/12)
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action + prev_state == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action + prev_state == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action + prev_state == 2) * (tv("action",-2) + tv("state",-2) == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action + prev_state == 2) * (tv("reward",-2) == 0) * np.exp(ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action + prev_state == 2) * ep_trial
explanation: Silent at GO and D2; at D1 it grows roughly exponentially with trial in the episode (timing baseline). Beyond timing, the magnitude is set by the previous trial: large after a1 reaching S1 (common), larger still when that trial was unrewarded, and suppressed after any trial reaching S2 or after a2->S1 (rare). The observer belief that S1 is good (belief_lo) adds a graded positive effect. All effects scale with an exp(ep_trial/10) envelope, i.e. are multiplicative with the late-episode ramp; linear-in-trial versions fit much worse. The free fit adds the trial before (another a1->S1, or unrewarded) and a separate a1 term, gaining about 0.1 R^2. Uses only observed quantities.

issues: The recorded short form has no plain D1*exp(ep_trial/10) term, so late in the episode it predicts activation after every previous-trial type, including ones where the feature is silent. Misses on it show systematic over-prediction at D1 after a1 S2 u (-0.21), a2 S2 u (-0.17), a1 S2 r (-0.15) and a2 S1 r (-0.13), plus a D1 phase mean error of -0.044. belief_lo*exp is partly standing in for this missing negative envelope; it is not mainly a graded belief effect.

Replacing belief_lo*exp with a plain (phase==D1)*exp(ep_trial/10) term raises test R^2 from 0.587 to 0.685, which already beats the claimed free fit (0.679). The two-term form [(prev a1->S1)*exp, D1*exp] alone scores 0.682 on test.

'More when unrewarded' is a small effect. Adding last_is('a1 S1 u')*exp to the two-term form gains only +0.003 test R^2 (0.682 -> 0.685), and its fitted weight is about 18% of the a1->S1 weight. A generic prev_reward==0 term adds +0.0005. The label overstates this point.

The claim that the short form reaches 86% of the free fit is wrong as stated, because the free fit itself is beaten by a 3-term short form. The free-fit extras (the trial before, a separate a1 term) each add under 0.01.

The remaining worst misses are occasional large activations (about 3) at D1 late in the episode after a rare trial (a2->S1 or a1->S2) that followed a run of a1->S1 trials. This is scattered, not a large systematic class.
With the envelope at exp(ep_trial/12), [a1->S1*exp, D1*exp, belief_lo*exp] gives test 0.705. belief_lo adds about 0.015 once the envelope is present, so it is a genuine but minor graded effect.
The claims 'silent at GO and D2' and 'raised after a1->S1 and low after S2 or a2->S1' check out (residual table and fits).
